name: Vanthorpe Analyst's Pressed Distinction Set
description: The Tier 4 specialist's answer to the corporate uniform — not a rebellion, but a negotiation. The trousers are Vanthorpe's own selvedge-weave wool-analog in deep charcoal, cut with a slightly higher rise and a subtly wider leg than regulation, landing exactly within the acceptable deviation window that every Tier 4 employee has memorized. The shirt is a Vanthorpe Coolweave in pale cream rather than the standard-issue blue, the collar structured without being stiff, the fabric visibly better — it drapes rather than sits. Over it goes a single-breasted blazer in a dark slate herringbone, not issued but purchased, with a half-lining in a deep copper-rust that flashes only when the wearer reaches for something. The left sleeve has a discreet aug-channel seam running from elbow to cuff, accommodating a chrome forearm prosthetic with a clean, unobtrusive split that closes magnetically when not needed. Footwear is a pair of Sorel & Vane cap-toe oxfords in oxblood, resoled once and better for it. A slim brushed-titanium BCI port cover at the right temple, matching the blazer buttons. No lanyard. Badge is embedded.
functionality: Aug-channel seam in left sleeve for chrome forearm compatibility, embedded badge RFID in blazer lining, BCI port cover integrated at temple, temperature-regulating coolweave shirt layer, magnetic closure aug-seam
what_it_says: You earn enough to choose your own clothes. You chose well but not provocatively. You know exactly where the line is and you have placed yourself one careful step on the correct side of it. The oxblood shoes are the tell — you have opinions, and you are confident enough to express one.
worn_by: anyone who has passed their second review cycle and knows it
manufacturer: Vanthorpe Ready-to-Wear (blazer and trousers); Vanthorpe Coolweave line (shirt); Sorel & Vane (footwear)
story_hooks: The copper-rust lining of this blazer is a color associated with a specific internal faction within a corponation — a color the wearer chose innocently. Suddenly they are receiving nods from people three tiers above them and cold shoulders from their own team.

The embedded badge in the blazer lining has been quietly cloned. Someone is walking floors they shouldn't be walking. The original owner doesn't know yet, but they've started getting flagged for access events they can't account for.

A character is being interviewed for a Tier 5 position. The interviewer spends thirty seconds looking at their shoes before saying anything. The oxblood oxfords were either exactly right or exactly wrong, and the character won't know which until the offer letter arrives — or doesn't.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A calculated departure from corporate conformity—sharp, composed, subtly individualized. The silhouette reads as polished professional with understated confidence: straight shoulders, a clean vertical line broken only by the strategic flash of copper-rust when the blazer moves. This is someone who has learned the exact millimeters of acceptable deviation.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored without appearing bespoke. Trousers sit with a slightly higher rise than standard-issue, leg cut just wide enough to signal intent without triggering oversight algorithms. Blazer is close-fitted through the torso, sleeves cut to accommodate aug hardware. The shirt drapes—expensive fabric language for 'not struggling to contain a body.'
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-analog selvedge-weave (trousers), premium Coolweave cotton-derivative (shirt), herringbone wool blend (blazer), brushed titanium hardware
physical_description.texture: Herringbone blazer reads with subtle visual texture even under flat light; shirt has a soft, almost liquid drape; trousers show the tight weave characteristic of selvedge construction. All surfaces project 'handled with intention,' not worn to softness—worn to purpose.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal trousers, pale cream shirt, dark slate herringbone blazer with a shocking copper-rust half-lining visible only in movement. Oxblood oxfords ground the palette. Brushed titanium catches ambient light without announcing itself.
physical_description.closures: Standard button front on blazer (titanium), magnetic snap aug-channel seam on left sleeve, traditional lacing on oxfords—no visible tech integration, all augmentation seamlessly accommodated
distinctive_features: Augmentation-channel seam running elbow to cuff on left sleeve with magnetic closure
Copper-rust half-lining that flashes only in motion—coded signal of careful individualism
Brushed-titanium BCI port cover at right temple, matching blazer buttons
Embedded security badge—no lanyard, no visible ID
Resoled oxfords showing one repair cycle—suggests either longevity or inability to replace
Selvedge-weave edges visible on trouser hems—subtle quality signal
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 aspirational—too refined for Tier 3 salvage culture, too intentional to be Tier 2 corpo-standard, too functional to be Tier 1 luxury display
physical_description.cultural_context: A specialist who has decoded the system: this outfit says 'I know the rules precisely well enough to bend them without breaking.' Worn by data architects, mid-level analysts, security specialists who interface with corporate infrastructure but retain agency in presentation. The augmentation visibility is professional, not flash.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine in all respects except the oxfords, which carry one visible resoling—everything else reads as deliberately maintained, purchased for specific function rather than status collection

image_prompt: Tier 4 corporate specialist in full analytical dress standing in a climate-controlled office overlooking the Great Lakes industrial zone at dusk. Moody cool-blue ambient light from massive windows casting long shadows across brushed concrete flooring. The model's left arm raised slightly, copper-rust lining of the blazer catching the last amber sunlight. Right temple shows the brushed-titanium BCI port cover. Herringbone texture of the blazer visible in sharp detail, oxblood oxfords positioned with slight weight forward—the posture of someone mid-thought. Dark minimal background, perhaps a single corporate branding element or window frame. The overall mood: controlled intelligence, meticulous deviation, the aesthetic of someone who has memorized acceptable variance. Cinematic lighting. --ar 2:3 --v 6
